facts.fact: 妹妹这条小蛇等姐姐把整段窝囊事讲完，自己却把图书馆里的事扣下不说。
facts.anchor: Jingling, the little snake, waited until Kiamling had recounted the whole sorry story, keeping back whatever the heck had happened in the library.

facts.fact: 然后她不紧不慢地说，钱是 Ng Choy 律师付的。
facts.anchor: Then, quite casually, she said, “Barrister Ng Choy paid them.”

facts.fact: 妹妹说 Hoi 只提一个条件：把仓库清空、重新刷一遍，因为当初是她弄坏的。
facts.anchor: “That was his one condition. That you properly clean out and paint the place, seeing that it was your fault it got wrecked in the first place.”

facts.fact: 破木箱全搬了出去，稻草贝壳耙过、地板一桶桶水刷过；至少走私的货已经不在了。
facts.anchor: She had carried out all the broken crates, raked the straw and shells and scrubbed the floors with buckets of water. At least the pirated goods were not here.

facts.fact: Hoi 第无数次说她漏了一块没刷。
facts.anchor: “You missed a bit,” Hoi said for about the fiftieth time.

facts.fact: 他没有替她擦脸，反手把一块湿抹布甩在她脸上。
facts.anchor: Instead he flung a wet rag at her. It slapped her rudely across the cheek.

facts.fact: Hoi 笑而不否认；他当年在班里就是躲柱子后面、往师父袍子里塞青蛙的活宝。
facts.anchor: Hoi gor laughed, not denying it. He had been the clown in class, hiding behind pillars and putting frogs in the sifu’s robes.

facts.fact: 她回想起来，那些苦日子里 Hoi 和 Jingling 一直都在。
facts.anchor: But come to think of it, Hoi gor and Jingling were always there.

facts.fact: 他抬起头，请她帮忙读一份文件。
facts.anchor: He looked up. “Will you help me read this?”

facts.fact: 文件写明那艘叫 The Arrow 的飞剪船交 Tsui Chihoi 照管，把一箱箱鸦片运往……她问他是不是签了。
facts.anchor: “‘The clipper known as The Arrow will be given into the care of Tsui Chihoi, to transport crates of opium to…’ Hoi gor, did you sign this?”

facts.fact: 他说这不过是份活儿，他需要钱。
facts.anchor: “It’s just a job. I needed the money.”

facts.fact: Hoi 皱着眉说，有人告发了他。
facts.anchor: “Someone reported me.” Hoi gor frowned.

facts.fact: 鸦片无处不在：从妓院到烟馆，从田里到气派的厅堂。
facts.anchor: Opium was everywhere. From the brothels to the dens, the fields to the grand pavilions.

facts.fact: 她没法把所有人都怪一遍：马先生、Madam Yau、祖母，连 Hoi 也算上。
facts.anchor: It was hard to disapprove of everyone: Mr Ma, Madam Yau, Por Por, Hoi gor even.

facts.fact: 他小臂上留着一道道早已长好的烧伤凸痕。
facts.anchor: Raised impressions of long-healed burns marked his forearms.

facts.fact: 他说她只是还没被迫做过难的选择。
facts.anchor: “No, I think you haven’t had to make the hard choices yet.”

facts.fact: 她拿"你能干出什么，杀人吗"当玩笑问出口。
facts.anchor: “What could you possibly have done, killed a man?”

facts.fact: Hoi 却像被人在肋骨间拧了一刀那样一缩。
facts.anchor: but Hoi gor flinched like she had twisted a blade between his ribs.

facts.fact: 他反问海盗和商人除了那一纸文书究竟差在哪里。
facts.anchor: “What exactly is the difference between a pirate and a merchant other than a piece of paper?”

facts.fact: 她想通了：答案在文武庙。
facts.anchor: “Man Mo temple. That’s where the answers are.”
